key_insight: DexPort introduces a portable, hand-held interface for collecting dexterous manipulation demonstrations. Its central idea is to make data collection more practical than full robot teleoperation while addressing limitations of human-only demonstrations.
problem_solved: Dexterous manipulation data is difficult to collect: teleoperation requires a complete robot setup and complex finger coordination, while human demonstrations require motion estimation and retargeting and do not directly supply robot actions.
method: Introduce DexPort as a portable, hand-held skill interface for dexterous hand data collection.
Target the gap between robot teleoperation and human demonstration workflows.
The supplied abstract is truncated; interface mechanics, action representation, and experimental validation are not available.
impact: More accessible demonstration collection could help practitioners build datasets for dexterous robot learning. Specific gains in data quality, collection efficiency, or policy performance cannot be established from the supplied excerpt.
visual_elements: Three-way comparison: robot teleoperation, human demonstrations, and DexPort.

paper_title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
paper_authors: Amber Xie, Jiawei Fu, Xiaofeng Guo, Carmelo Sferrazza, Guanya Shi
